patterns.pattern: Users' access to dashboards, records, or cases is controlled by roles, group membership, or explicit permissions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Access to dashboards and cases is determined by user roles and group assignments.

patterns.pattern: Admins, administrators, or superusers have elevated or unrestricted access to management, user, and configuration features.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only admins and superusers can manage users, records, and advanced settings.

patterns.pattern: Items, records, users, or entities must have unique identifiers within their defined scope.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each user, case, or item must have a unique ID within the system.

patterns.pattern: Access to sensitive or embargoed items/files/fields is restricted; only authorized users can access full content.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only authorized users may view files in embargoed items; others see metadata only.

patterns.pattern: Audit trails/logs must be recorded for all modifications and access, be unalterable, and retained for a required period.
patterns.example_phrasing: All actions and access attempts are logged; audit logs cannot be changed or deleted.

patterns.pattern: Only users with certain roles or permissions can create, modify, or delete records or content.
patterns.example_phrasing: Only authorized users can add, update, or delete records.

patterns.pattern: Records with dependencies/child records cannot be deleted until all dependencies are resolved.
patterns.example_phrasing: Records cannot be deleted if there are linked child records.

patterns.pattern: Permissions are inherited or can be cascaded through collections, groups, or organization structure, with the most permissive/granular applying.
patterns.example_phrasing: Permissions cascade from parent to child collections; the most permissive among group memberships applies.

patterns.pattern: Files/data items can be shared publicly only if the item is explicitly released, made public, or the link is issued to external users.
patterns.example_phrasing: Public sharing of dashboards or records requires explicit release or a secret shareable link.

patterns.pattern: Mandatory fields must be completed for certain transactions or entity creation.
patterns.example_phrasing: All required fields must be completed when creating a user or transaction.

patterns.pattern: All changes or important events must be communicated to relevant users, e.g. release notes, plan review outcomes, or audit actions.
patterns.example_phrasing: Users are notified of outcomes or changes, such as release notes and plan reviews.

patterns.pattern: Application, case, or process stages/lifecycles must be followed in a defined sequence and preconditions must be met before advancing.
patterns.example_phrasing: Applicants must complete required steps before proceeding to the next case stage.

patterns.pattern: Direct data/file/database access by end users is not allowed; interactions happen via GUI or defined interfaces.
patterns.example_phrasing: Users cannot access data or files except via the app interface.

patterns.pattern: Certain actions or features (upload, raw HTML, configuration) are restricted or require explicit enabling by an admin.
patterns.example_phrasing: Some features require admin enabling before users can access them.

patterns.pattern: Version history or changes of items, dashboards, or cases are recorded for rollback or audit.
patterns.example_phrasing: Dashboards and object versions are recorded and can be restored by managers.

patterns.pattern: Role, group, or division attributes must be assigned when creating a user or entity.
patterns.example_phrasing: Each user must have at least one role, group, and division assigned at creation.

patterns.pattern: Configurable security responses or access controls for unauthorized actions or case access.
patterns.example_phrasing: System can be configured to control how unauthorized case access is handled.

patterns.pattern: Compliance with relevant external or organizational standards is required (accessibility, regulatory, etc.).
patterns.example_phrasing: System must comply with WCAG and regulatory standards like HIPAA and FDA.

patterns.pattern: Linked entities (e.g., specimens, samples) must maintain referential integrity (all links valid, nothing orphaned).
patterns.example_phrasing: Each sample must be linked to a subject and valid test request.

patterns.pattern: Duplicate data entries (e.g., dispute requests, IDs) are automatically prevented or rejected.
patterns.example_phrasing: Duplicate dispute requests or IDs are not allowed in the system.
